The transmitter is the nicest tx of any RTF kit I've experienced in the micro fixed pitch flybarless world. By far. A big LED display, nice stick action, a real good metal handle, 2 speeds, mode 2 operation. The helicopter itself is in a class of its own in my experience. Spools up completely vertically, fast as a V944, but way better handling and with precise maneuverability. Its a heavy weight and flies beautifully straight and true in good 10mph winds unaffected. I can fly it as if it were a V911 or a Syma F3 in still air. You'd swear it had a flybar, except it's so fast! She's a heavy gal but the main motor handles the 54g with aplomb, and the weight makes her great in the wind. She has enclosed rotary servos which are unusually quick for this type. Pirouettes- tail in or tail out, stops on a dime, incredible climbs and dives and banks. You'd think I was an intermediate pilot or flying a flybarred micro. Really long flights of up to 8 min. About 2x the length of flights for my HFP80 or MSRx or V944 with their standard batteries. I am spoiled now.I received a white one, which is good for my tired eyes. The canopy was dull, I gave it a good clear coat, now it looks fine. The white main and tail rotor blades really are visible for me as well. Seeing the blade disc's orientation has never been easier. The green looks much much nicer on the shelf however.I also fly the Blade MSRx, HiSky HFP80, WLtoys V944, and the ESKY 150 as well and they are all wonderful to master, but it's a fact that the YD-117 beats them all in ease of flying, flight time length, and maneuverability. Everything really. I am still astounded. Get extra 380mah, 20c  battery packs.It's really a hefty, well built, sturdy bird: strong landing gear, stout frame, thick carbon fiber tail boom, thick gauge plastic for the canopy, meaty tail motor cage.I recommend trying it.[...]

reviewText: I have had so much fun with my 9100's- I have crashed the first one many times and broke just about all parts that make it go.When I first started learning I soon realized I was going to need a variety of parts. For the most part I bought mine a piece at a time and was wishing there was a quick ware spare parts pack available. After some time I began to see some of these packages advertised. A great way to get your parts and save some on cost especially shipping. This package contains just about every part that I broke except for the blades. Now they are banged up with dents but still work fine.If you fly the 9100, you will sooner or later need some of the parts. Buy you up some while they are available, because they may be gone later.I have several reviews on the 9100 and it's many parts. Look back at them and they may help you if you are having some problems. My first copter I had a lot of problems with it, but my second I have had no problems and it's still like new.Seems like when I read some of the reviews I have had some of the same issues. As for these SMALL plastic playing figures... When I was a young boy in the 1960's most of the toy products for boys like myself were geared towards violence or violent thinking. We had our little green army men everywhere and it was one of the biggest selling items for young boys (not a surprise since the Viet Nam WAR was going full blast at the time). We also had Cowboys and Indians as well... with horses for some. Of course some were extremely lucky to find Astronaut figures but they were NOT as easy to find as the others that I mentioned already and personally I never knew they existed until I grew up. It was all about being a soldier, cowboy, indian or a policeman as far as toys for us while growing up. I eventually joined the Military and have often wished that I had different toys or products to play with as a young child. If I could do it again I'd like a telescope to study the stars. I am a BIG believer that the children of today will grow up affected by the toys they play with as a child. I also think that it is no coincidence that toy market sell what they do in order to influence the future of children. I applaud parent who offer peaceful toys to thier children... and especially parents who offer thier children items and life experiences which help the child grow strong in mind and body towards peaceful pursuits that far surpass what the parents themselves achieved. Our future needs more children who grow up with knowledge of the arts, science and that are socially active towards helping people. The future is inside the hearts and minds of the children of today... and unless we help them grow towards positive areas... we shall all reap what remains.

While certainly not as stealthy as other Nerf guns, the portability and rail/stock options for this weapon can transform it from a simple rapid fire hand gun to a semi-auto SMG.  The gun is noticably heavier (3 AA's don't help) than most nerf handhelds and the long, akward barrel (designed to prevent fingers from contacting the spinning motor) detracts from an overall sleek appearance.  The placement of the "On" switch is excellent, unless you are left handed (sorry south-paws).  Reloading is the biggest trial, as the chamber (a rotating barrel of 10 slots) can only be loaded when rotated in the "open" position and this position can only be achieved while the motor is on (there is a catch door on the top of the weapon that can be opened which will prevent the motor from spinning but still allow rotation of the barrel with the trigger).  At most only 6 of the 10 slots in the chamber can be visible for reloading (and 2 of those 6 are awkwardly positioned and the darts need to be bent slightly to enter).  The motor can launch the darts with considerable energy, but it also sounds much like a small vacuum cleaner even from 20 feet away.Despite shortcomings in overall appearance and the main detractor of creating a great deal of noise before firing, this Nerf gun can deliver a substantial number of darts on a target with realtive ease and fair accuracy and almost no effort.
summary: Very loud, but very durable and fast

When I first purchased the car it was pretty frustrating due to the fact that the iPad 3rd Gen would rarely register it on the screen. After thorough observation there are several limiting factors to the car's ability to penetrate properly on the iPad's screen. Fortunately it only requires 1 simple modification to solve all of these. Screen protectors, magnetic cases, and other protective devices are the main limiting factors. I debated taking my screen protector off and seeing if that would make a difference but then decided I would rather modify the cheap car & take it back if it still didn't work.Guess what.... It turns out that the three contact points on the bottom of the cars have a plastic wrapper/shield covering them and the pull off easily with a finger nail. Don't use a knife or any tool as you will risk marring the surface of the contact point which would cause sharp burrs. Just pull the covers off with your fingernail and begin enjoying the game with any case or screen protector. I tried all of my cases & I have a bunch!The contacts are super smooth without the wrapper & to be honest I am thinking it was supposed to be just a shipping seal. Once removed they are more like a plastic wrapper than a anti-scratching material. I really couldn't believe the difference... My daughter can grab anywhere on the car & it never looses signal with the iPad!I'd recommend only removing the plastic if you have a screen protector, although I don't personally feel it would scratch the screen without it. The plastic covers pull very easily off which makes me think they were originally supposed to be taken off.... Who knows
summary: Works Flawlessly with 1 Quick & Simple Mod

reviewText: I have not yet purchased this product, although I have played it multiple times. I'm waiting for theexpansions to buy them together, and can't wait! ;) That being said...Lords of Waterdeep is an amazing game in the Euro Resource Style. My wife has never been a D&D;player, but as a huge fan of Ticket to Ride, Carcassonne she loves this game. As a D&D; player I wasnever particularly into Forgotten Realms, so I have little understanding of the setting. The game isamazingly entertaining for my wife, me and my friends as the setting never gets in the way, but oftenadds interesting flavor. The games playability by non D&D; fans is a testament to its amazing design.From a game mechanics standpoint Lords of Waterdeep adds a critical game mechanic to resource styleboard games. It means that the first player can change for each of the 10 rounds of play. The ability toplay an agent and gain the first play next turn is crucial to planning strategy in a resource style boardgame. This is a brilliant mechanic that needs to be included in future resource style games.The perspective change from first person to third person is going to be a little mind blowing for any D&D;RPG player; mind blowing in a good way. Something like what it was like to play Magic: the Gatheringfor the first time. The game is a whole new perspective on classic RPG concepts. It's tempting toreverse engineer a new way to play RPG's from this 3rd person perspective...
summary: Great board game, D&D fan not required.

When my students approach my desk, they inevitably want to touch and play with the things on it, which sometimes is a problem. This Zen Garden was my solution to this problem. Its so predictable and sweet; a student will stand at my desk, pick up the little rake and start drawing in the sand and say to me, "Miss, what's this thing for?" I always smile and reply, "Just what you are doing right now." A few have made me laugh as they continue to draw and design in the sand and say, "Well that's dumb." To which I reply, "You're STILL doing it, aren't you?" :-)I think there is something primal about playing with sand and it has brought joy to my classroom - to my students who now have a little toy and to me because they now have something they should be touching on my desk, and of course the smiles they give me when they do play with it!Is this the best one out there? No, not really. It is a little cheap. One of the legs came off, but I glued it back on. Also, its not very deep, I have to keep the whole thing in the tray that it came it to prevent sand spillage all over my desk - fortunately the box it came in has a nice black cardboard tray that doesn't detract from its appearance. This bottom is also helpful because the wooden garden itself isn't 100% level. The sand is very fine, so it leaves a powder residue around the frame - I use a small make up brush to brush this sand back into the garden.So, no it is not the best one out there, but it does do what its supposed to do and between the rocks and two garden tools it comes with (which have held up well so far - 3 months of use), it is a nice starter set at a decent price. Also, the book that contains the meditations is lovely and a nice part of the set.I had some pretty tumbled rocks I had from when I taught science and replaced the plain brown ones with them and it looks great.

And, heck, at about $2-4 per pet, I save a fortune over those "not-so-happy meals."There are a few quirky drawbacks... (1) These adorable bobbleheads can be addictive... finding them at different retailers begins to feel like a (fun) scavenger hunt.  That's fun doing it that way, but now Ebay sellers seem to be buying up all they can (at the price point fit for a child's small allowance) and CHARGING double to 10 times retail as they try to create a new "beanie baby debacle" out of this toy that should be PLAYED WITH rather than scooped up by adults to make an extra $5.(2) Because growing the collection is so fun, you can outgrow the limited space in the Playhouse quickly... meaning you might want to plan on the Whirly-twirly playground thingy right from the beginning.  Just expect it and set aside the $30 for your collection to grow... because it will.  Oh, yes, it surely will!  :)

I purchased a number of Phalanx Games since many are being discontinued.One of the ones I came across was "The Prince" by Alexander Berg.This game moved from the "Play Soon" Pile to the "Play Sometime" Pile to the "Where did I put that again?" Pile. I just pulled it out magically last night and started playing it.First, the game takes longer than the listed time amount on the box. Its listed as being 30-45 Minutes per game turns (Three game turns in an entire game), and the entire game took us about 5 hours. I can see the game will move faster when we know it better, we had to keep referring to the rules and figuring out what each card did, etc.As a second matter, like many of the Phalanx Games from Europe marketed by Mayfair, the rules have a vagueness to them and they are hard to really compose into a coherent set of rules. I think we got it pretty close though.I am told "The Prince" is reminiscent of "Junta". I'll take my wife's word on the matter as I haven't ever played "Junta"Each player starts with a specified number of cards, cardinals and money. Cardinals represent voting and political power, money is used to activate the powers of certain cards, and primarily for bidding on additional cards. Each turn consists of 12 cards to be auctioned off. One turn lasts then, therefore 12 player turns. The cards have specific actions, many cards must be played immediately, and most of the cards that don't need to be played immediately require a cost to use. The most common cards are "soldier" cards that add to the attack and defense of players that are undergoing (or instigating) attacks against other players.A couple of additional cards like "Accusation of Simonry" and "Savonarola" are quite a humorous break in the game. Accusing the current pope of Simonry is quite comedic.The individual victory point tracks are quite nasty and precarious, easy to knock over. The materials that make up the game are kinda thin and lackluster. The coins are of only three models, with different numbers on, which is hard to see to figure out what the denomination of the coin actually is.Overall, the game is quite fun and incorporates Machiavellian tactics and strategy and trying to trick other players. The variation of allowing wheedling, threats and negotiations I think increase the amount of time the game takes to play, but increases the amount of intricacy in negotiations. A deft and subtle diplomacy seems to be the order of the day for succeeding in "The Prince".Recommended.

The HS-82MG and the counterpart the HS-81 are great servos for their size and weight class (there's a new 82HB in the works).  These are Analog servos, the Digital versions have 4 digit names, so for example the digital version of this servo is HS-5082.  The digital versions have higher resolution and are important to use in critical areas such as tail accuracy on a Helicopter.  For most general purpose flying, analog servos work great.I use a lot of servos.  Keeping a dozen planes and gliders in flyable states causes me to continually build, rebuild and evaluate my servos so I write with the experience of many years.  The HS-82MG is one of my favorite for larger flaps on larger than 2m gliders.  It's slightly larger than the HS-65MG servo but much more powerful.  One installation issue is that you'll have to watch the servo width depending on your wing thickness to make sure it fits in there.  I have had less success with the HS-81, as I've tended to strip those gears so I stick with the MG version.This Metal Geared (MG) servo weighs 19 grams and has 2.8kg of torque at 4.8v and 3.4kg of torque at 6.0v.  In general the MG servos are stronger but have a bit more play than the HB gears do.  Due to these subtle differences, I pick which to use in any given situation based on how the servos will be abused.  For Glider Flaps where the gears are often stripped due to dragging on the ground during the landing, I use the MG servos.  For the more sensitive Ailerons, I prefer the HB servos that maintain tighter gears and thus more accurate control.  For the rudder usually use MG servos on planes with motors, HB on gliders.  On planes with motors, especially 3D planes with large rudders the Prop Wash is significant and the MG servos hold up really well.  I've also blown out plastic servos by bumping the large rudder via hangar rash (aka non-flying accidents).These servos come with a plus shaped control horn attached and then a double and single arm servo in the box.  They also come with four small flanged mounting screws.I'm sure you've seen the lower cost copies out there.  Let me explain why, even though they may be lower in price, it'll be more difficult to use those.1 They have less reliable quality control.  Sometimes whole batches of the off brand servos are bad and once you've got it in your plane they can be a real pain to change out.2 These servos are more accurate, center better and are more precise in their movements.3 Do you use and toss your gear or do you re-use it?  If you re-use things you really want servos that you know you can get parts for .  Hitec sells servo gears, screws, horns etc so you can change broken pieces out as necessary.4 when you need a special longer horn or special piece you know you can get that for your Hitec servos.  That is not the case for many of the after-market servos.I have tried the lower cost servos and over time, it has been proven to me time and time again to stick with the name brands to get the support and parts I need.  Hitec is amazing for their support; I did have one servo act weird in a rudder for me (it would wag with strong prop wash in big 3D moves.  I sent it in to Hitec with a note and they promptly sent me a new one, even though they could not duplicate the issue.5 stars, this is a great servo for a fair price and you'll enjoy these in your planes and gliders
summary: Reliable, powerful servo, great for small but strong planes (82MG)

reviewText: I first bought it when my daughter was only 3 years old.  She played with it once every few days, and got bored of it quickly each time within a few minutes.  She had no patient to wait for the spoken words to complete, and would rather scratch the book with the pen, making incoherent sounds in the process. The book that came with the pen was a bit too overwhelming for her as it contains games about rhymes and phonics, which are at a 5 year old level.Then over time, my daughter came back to it more and more, especially with the additional 3 books I bought for her.  She started out learning about the sound each picture makes, then the sound each word makes, and then (half a year later) how to play games.  The games themselves have 3 levels, which are appropriate for kids of different ages.  At 4 year old now, my daughter could play level 2 by herself, and needed a lot of help from me for level 3.So if your kid doesn't like it initially, just give it time.My daughter learned many new words from the book.  She also memorized a lot of phrases from the pen.  She has a knack of saying what the pen gonna say, then point the pen and made it say the same thing.The concept of this book is nothing short of a revolution.  What it gives beyond a normal book is the level of interactivity.  The level of interactivity can be very complex, much like the way human interact with one another.  For example, the book could ask the kid to find 4 pictures of the Flounder fish.  She clicks on the first one, it confirms by counting out loud "one", then she clicks on the second and it confirms "two", ... and after the last one it would say "good job".  That's not just teaching the kid how to count, but also interactive communication.  The constant feedback keeps the kids motivated in exploring and learning.The tag system also helps me (the parent) interacting with my kid more often.  My daughter constantly needs help with the games, and constantly tells me about the new things she discovered in the book.  Every time I bought her a new tag book, she would choose it as our bedtime story book, for several nights in a row.  If you want some me-time, this ain't the product to buy.I also bought for my daughter the Leapfrog Leapster hand-held video console.  While the Leapster is very interactive by itself, my daughter doesn't like it as much.  The book has much better graphics that the tiny low-resolution screen on the Leapster can't compare.  The physical touch  and feel of the book pages is also much more intuitive for kids.Other info for parents:The tip of the Tag pen is as sharp as a normal pen, so don't give it to kids below 3 year old, in case they poke their eyes out.The books are quite expensive compared to normal books, but what you're paying is also the voices, sound effects and games too.The Tag pen shuts down when not used for 5 minutes by itself to save battery, as kids often forget to turn it off.  The two AAA batteries do last a reasonable amount time, although I use rechargeable batteries anyways since I already have them.You must have internet connection and USB port on your computer to be able to download voices for new books.  The software fine for both Windows XP 32-bits and Windows 7 64-bits.  Although I can't store too many stories into the pen, it's rather easy to transfer them in and out using the computer software.As far as durability, it's been working fine.  The painted symbols on some buttons are rubbing off.
summary: Revolutionary toy - slowly became my kid's favorite

reviewText: This switch and go dino is another one we added to my 4 year old son's collection.  He got a few for for Christmas and loves to play with them.  He calls them robot dinosaurs, although they actually convert into cars and then dinos.  I guess they are somewhat robotic looking.  Anyhow, he picked up the transformation between the two forms almost immediately- and he'll actually spend a lot of the time playing with them just converting back and forth.  He's fascinated by how it works.  My husband was trying to convert one of these and he struggled to figure out the order- but my son was able to help him.  LOL!  These remind us of the transformers us parents used to have.These are durable and although they have some sharp edges, even my 1 year old seems to be safe with them.  Although the question for most toys in our house is whether the toy is safe from him.  ;-)  What we do when he wants to play too is convert to a car and let him use that so that none of the pieces are really sticking out or breakable.This stompsalot version lights up with a red light on it's head and it also speaks a few terms which it will repeat.  The other versions that we had before have more of a simple screen that flashes simple designs while it talks.  I feel like those versions are even more durable, more random in their speaking, have a friendlier male voice who is the race car driver (the voice for this one sounds like an erudite professor), and almost seem to interact with each other (not sure if they do though- but my son thinks they do).Although this blue one almost seems more detailed in a way, it also makes it more likely for a piece to break off in my opinion.  The other ones seem clunkier (in a good way) which works for a younger child.Overall, still a cute idea which my son enjoys.  Just compare the available options as you shop to make sure you get the ones that best fit your child.
summary: Super cool, but the other versions are cooler

This is an interesting wire or disentanglement puzzle.I chose my title from the fact that this puzzle actually goes by at least two names.Also here on Amazon ,it is offered as Mantis Wire puzzle,by Winshare.Actually ,I kind of like that name.It's natural to give these wire puzzles names,and that is often very difficult.In this case ,when you look at the puzzle spread out,it does resemble the face of a lion.However,it just as well resembles the face of a Praying Mantis.So,pick your choice--I guess.It is well made of nickle plated wire and fairly sturdy;but could be bent out of shape by the use of excessive force.As with all wire puzzles,the solution definately does not require excessive force.It is complicated,even a bit intimidating when you first look at it;and it is actually of medium difficulty to solve.If you get too frustrated and need a little assistance in solving it;you can ask Puzzlemaster to e-mail you a solution,or even go to You-Tube where you can see it being solved.Sometimes, brainteasers can really have you stumped,because once you have tried everything you can think of ,and are not able to come up with the "secret"to solving it,there is no reason not to get a little help.Once you have solved any puzzle,all is not lost;because all you have to do is put it away for a while,and it becomes a challenge all over again.This is a good puzzle more suitable for people who have some experience with brainteasers rather than a beginner.

This is an Optimus Prime toy that is both fun but can also be frustrating.  Let me outline what I see are the pros and cons of this figure.Pros:* Intuitive transformation.  After going through the instructions and figuring out the basic transformation scheme, going back through it repeatedly is both intuitive and fun.* Clicky joints.  LOTS of clicky joints.  Almost every joint on this figure is a ratcheting joint with plenty of adjustment allowing Prime to get a lot of great poses in.Articulation.  Points of articulation are (R is for ratcheting):- Shoulder rotation and lift (R) - universal joint not ball.- Head is on ball joint- Bicep swivel at elbow- Thumb swivel - yeah, there's a thumb swivel here; a random but cool addition.- Elbow (R)- Waist- Hips (universal again both with R)- Thigh swivel at knee- Knees (R)- Ankle tilt/twist (not a ton there but still some)* Chrome - Hasbro seems to be in love with chrome these days, and not just chrome but oodles of it in weird places.  This figure has it tastefully done and in places you'd expect it.  Gas tanks, exhaust pipes, grill.  My 6yo son absolutely loves the chrome so it's a definite plus for kids.- Rubber tires and fully pinned wheels.  This is a toy that rolls really smoothly in truck mode.  Probably my favorite feature of the figure.- Weapon storage in truck mode.  Shield pegs onto the truck hitch and sword is slotted underneath.- Truck mode is really good.  All those panels make up a licensed truck mode that looks just like it's movie depiction.Cons:* Kibble.  The entire wheelbase is hanging off the back of Optimus.* Panels are terribly restrictive but do need to be readjusted every time a new pose is set.* Instructions.  I'm not sure how Hasbro has found a way to do it, but the new instructions are just brutally bad.  And to top it off they only go one way, from truck to robot while the toy is packaged as a robot.  That first transformation can be a real challenge because of this.  Luckily it is a MUCH easier go after that first time.Summary:This is a good toy with some very good play value.  It definitely helps that Hasbro is now indicating that the figure is designed for kids older than 5 as an 8yo should be perfectly capable transforming and playing with it.  For collectors this is probably the better of the Optimus figures after Evasion Optimus.
summary: Fun Optimus but not without some issues

Never before have I been so happy about playing a card game.That being said I'm not a huge LCG or CCG fan.Also, this isn't really a card game: it's a game WITH cards.Summoner wars plays much like a dice based combat miniatures game, with the strategy of deck based card games where you have to plan for what is ahead in your deck. Also, Chess.There are tons of videos and reviews that describe how this game is played so I won't do that. You can even download the rulebook off of Plaid Hats website.No doubt this is a great game so instead I will talk about what I really like, and what I'm not a fan of.CAUTION: I'm really nit picky about components.+Pros+This is super accessible: Rules are super easy to explain and all the cards explain themselves.The card art is great: it's my style of art.The box is BIG: You can fit your kids in there.The board is great quality: Nice and slick for sliding cards around.-Cons-The Box is BIG: You can lose your kids in there. Also, it's hard to take around for just a card game. There are many different storing alternatives though.The dice are bad: They are blah dice. Boring. I would love some SW themed dice.The cards are American shape: Meaning that no stores around me sell sleeves for them. (Order Mayday Chimera).If you sleeve the cards they don't fit in the box: Well actually they might depending on the sleeve.Notice how all the cons are super nit picky stuff, but that isn't too uncommon among board gamers. These quips do not detract from the fantastic PvP experience this game provides.If you are on the fence about this game, don't be.Buy it.It's a great game from a great company.

I saw this game advertised as winning a 'Major Fun Award' and you can bet your bottom dollar, this game is major fun.  You cannot help but have fun playing Catch 22.  As the name suggests, you need to catch 22 chips and exit the game board to win.  But, also as the name suggests, you might find yourself in a 'Catch 22' situation.  For example, once you win alot of chips, everybody else is going to try and catch you to steal your chips.  Or, a player might land on a switch places square and when you thought you were home free, you are forced to switch places with an opponent.  The strategy part is that you have 'Blocker Cubes' to try and clear a path for yourself or indeed block an opponents path.  But be careful, you only have five cubes and once you use them up, you must land on a square which allows you to collect a blocker cube from the board.  This is simply a fantastic game.  It is fast moving and heart stopping.  I cannot tell you how many times someone was on the verge of winning and in a heart beat, all their chips were stolen. Really, you should definitely try this game, I highly recommend it if you are into having fun.

I thought this would be an automatic 5-star figure. We've been waiting for a super-articulated Aliens version of the Xenomorph for years now. NECA overall did a great job. But it's not a 5-star figure, at least not the one I got.First, NECA added a lot of new features making this pretty much a brand new figure. It is NOT a rerelease of the previous one. Some of the new features include double-jointed elbows and knees, flexible dorsal fin and pipes, and a slimy coat of brown varnish.So, what's not to like. On the one I got, there were a lot of quality control issues with regard to the paint. Mine had a large dollop of silver paint on his forehead. I scratched most of it off, but you can still tell that there's some silver paint left. There are a few other parts of the figure which have sloppy paint jobs. I can understand small areas but to have a big drop of silver on his forehead is simply unacceptable. If you buy yours in the store, inspect the figure carefully!On a more general note, the figure doesn't stand very well. The legs have a lot of articulation, but the figure has no center of balance. You can either stand him fully erect, which the Aliens never do, or you can have him squatting. The squatting pose looks better but took a lot of work to get right. The trick is to use the tail as a "third leg" to support his weight.Overall, this is a great figure, and I probably just had an unfortunate experience. I'd just like to think that NECA is beyond these quality control issues nowadays.
summary: close to 5, but for quality control

I noticed that a lot of the low ratings were because people found the taggers too complex to use, or hard to aim, or too many buttons. Note that the toys (by Hasbro, NOT Toymaxx, which is Laser Challenge) are for children 8 and up. Any kid younger than that will need adult assistance. Also note that you don't HAVE to use the complex stuff. If you want a quick game of tag, just pull the trigger twice (once to turn it on, then again to start LTAG mode), and you're off with a 10 second countdown. To play more complex games, hosting is necessary, but it's really not that hard. One person hosts the game (the oldest kid or the adult), and the rest just choose "Join" and hit the OK button a couple times. Wait a few seconds until each player gets the "You're in!" indicator, and then the host can press 2ndF and OK to skip the 60 second counter to start. Then there's the 30 second timer to get ready so that everyone has time to take their position before the game starts. It ain't rocket science.As for the sights on the Deluxes, yeah, they suck. But Hasbro just released the 2-Pack Accessory Kit that comes with a new "Virtual Scope" sight, which is REALLY good, and a must have for the Deluxe taggers. The Thunder Pack is really cool, too. But, if you don't have any LTTO, or want to add more to your collection, get the new IRT-2X. It has sights on the top and is much easier and more natural to aim with. The Virtual Scope works with it, too, but it's not as needed as with the Deluxe. The IRT-2X has some new games for hosting as well.Finally, the whole indoor/outdoor thing. LTTO has a VERY long range. When playing indoors, it's VITAL to switch it to indoor mode to reduce the range and sensitivity. Most houses have walls that reflect infrared light really well. When you fire an LTTO tagger inside, the signal will bounce all over the place, and tag anything in the same room, especially in outdoor mode. In indoor mode, this is less of a problem. LTTO is also very precise for a laser tag system, and you really do need to aim to land a tag at any distance outdoors. Learning to aim is vital to landing lots of tags, so take a few minutes to make sure everyone playing knows how to aim with the tagger they have.Anyway, people need to stop buying this for 5 year olds and stuff. For the little kids, something cheap and lame like Laser Challenge is better. LTTO is for big kids, teens, and adults... the ones who actually play for more than 5 minutes, and care about features and quality.
summary: Notes for those who read bad reviews...

My hat comes off to those designers at Takara, Masterpiece Skywarp is one excellent piece of engineering.Originally, I was looking for MP Starscream, but since stocks were short and the only one left costs twice as much as Skywarp, I settled for Skywarp instead, I could accept black. Anyway, the awesome detail of this toy is truly unprecedented, in both F-15 and human form, Skywarp (and Starscream for that matter) looks unbelievably realistic. I've transformed him into human form, put him up on the stand, and I can't take my eyes off him!This toy is obviously not for kids, it is a piece of precision engineering which takes patience and care to transform. It is meant to be looked at, to be admired. While not built for durability, love and care can ensure him last through the years.He comes with Sidewinders and laser cannons, pilot, stand and decals. Transforming him with care takes around 20 to 25 minutes. The only flaw is that when in F-15 mode, a section of the spine (immediately behind the cockpit) sticks out, no matter how you try to push it back into position, it sticks out again. A picture of the jet mode in the instruction manual shows this section sticking out as well, so its no doubt a common design/manufacturing flaw. Still overall, this is a very impressive toy, and I look forward to more MPs.

I took it apart and measured it to see if the seller sent the wrong size.  Because the bracelt fits into the clasp, when connected you lose 1/2 an inch of the bracelet's length.  Disconnected and laid out flat the bracelet was just under 5 inches long.  Plus you need to consider that the beads are going to reduce the diameter as well.  I feel miffed at the seller because a bracelet meant for removeable beads should never be made small enough to fit a toddler.  Invariably a mom will buy one for her toddler who could then choke. I'm surprised it hasn't been "recalled" yet.  Now I have a bracelet that won't fit any child old enough to wear it and only a few days to go before her birthday. I did turn around and order the 6 inch and 6 1/2 inch b/c I already bought the beads to adorn it.  The clasp and bracelet are otherwise well made considering the very inexpensive price. I ordered this ring as a replacement for a different spinner ring I lost. I'm neither overly pleased nor disappointed with this ring. Remember you get what you paid for.-As noted in other reviews, the red and orange crystals are the exact same color. There is no difference between the two, so if red's your favorite color, you're good. If orange is your favorite color, you're sol. Also, the green crystal is actually a deeper forest green, and the indigo crystal is a light pink. The only colors that are even close to true on the image are the yellow, red, and blue.-The stones do stand out from the band, so it is slightly textured. If you're buying for an inner finger, beware. I bought this for my index finger, and the texture doesn't bother me much, but it could bother people with more sensitive skin.-The quality of the ring is obvious in the price. When I first pulled it out, it took a bit of elbow grease to get it to spin. I got this ring as something to fidget with that wouldn't be clicking or tapping pens, so 24 hours later it spins okay. After a bit more wear, it will likely spin even better, but be warned, it is cheap craftsmanship. It may not spin well right out of the box, and it will squeak until you break it in.-As far as losing gems, as earlier reviews commented, I haven't lost any yet. The gems aren't set consistently into the band, though. Some are set deeper than others; again the quality shows through. This will probably lead to some of the shallower gems falling out eventually. When that happens, I'll probably do what an earlier reviewer suggested and fill the missing slots with nail polish.-The band also runs about a quarter size small. My index finger is a size 12, measured by a handful of jewelers in the past, and all the rings I'd purchased from said jewelers still fit. This ring is tight enough that I have to work to put it on and take it off. Again, a reflection of the craftsmanship.Despite the above drawbacks, I'm okay with the ring. It's a cheap replacement for a trinket I use to amuse myself when I'm bored, to help myself pay attention in lectures and meetings, and to keep my hands busy so I can focus while I'm thinking. And the gems catch the light prettily, even if orange is missing.

It is not smooth and buttery like Coach's glove tanned leather nor is it soft but thin like cheap leather.  It is relatively thick and feels more artisanal and less mass-produced.Here are my issues with this bag:- No organization feature - The front pocket under the two buckles does not have any zippers so you can only put things in there that you don't care too much if they slip out and are lost.  There is only one small inside pocket to put my wallet.  I must put my other small items - Blackberry & pens, etc. in the large compartment.  It is very challenging to locate these items once the bag is full of files and such.- Flimsy and not adjustable strap - The included strap is quite thin and you cannot adjust its length.  It really would have been better to make the handles a bit longer so I can just carry the bag by the handles and not use the strap all-together.This is a pretty bag with European flair.  However, it is not the ideal commute bag due to the lack of organization features and the flimsy strap.  It probably would be better to use this bag as an overnight bag than an everyday commute bag.
summary: Nice leather, good size but no organization feature

reviewText: Found this review on another site and thought about sharing it here as there are very few reviews out there and this one is a quality review:"The Plano is a much needed revision to the older Alto jacket that used the same weaving of SOFtech fabric. I'm not a fan of SOFtech for outdoors pursuits since it is not breathable, heavy, quick-to-get-dirty, and has a canvas burlap stiffness to it. For casual around town I find that these SOFtech jackets are uncomfortable since they are not windstopper proof and you will get cold on chilly windy 35 F-and below days. The tight armpits and slim cut makes layering difficult unless you have a rock star thin body.Wear the Plano in anything warmer and sunnier than 50 F degrees the thing becomes an two ton oven on your back.Also the price of Mammut's SOFtech is greater than the price of other better fitting and more wind and weather protective technical jackets from other brands. Mammut wants $199 and up for the Plano when even Mammut's own Ultimate Pro or Ultimate Hoody Jackets are a much more superior piece for about the same price. This is like Mercedes Benz selling their economy A Class hatchback mini car for the same price as the S63 AMG Sports Saloon.It makes no sense to me especially when the Plano/Alto jackets are not well tailored and are not technical jackets like everything else Mammut makes. Beyond looking good when you try them on in the store the Plano/Alto certainly did not feel good for me.The main negative is the lack of sleeve articulation so the stiff SOFtech fabric bunches up around your torso when moving your arms about.That said, the Plano does try to improves on the fit over the Alto by making the sleeves a reasonable length and girth relative to the torso. Mammut also made the cuff cinch system much better than the absymal plastic ones the Alto had. However the neck protection on the Plano jacket is not better than the Alto so getting a European Hooded version Plano(Which is an update from the Mammut Heron Hoody-which coincidentally was the hooded companion to the Alto) is the way to go there.The pockets are narrow and tight fitting and the Plano has no pit zip ventilation although the pockets are now high enough (relative to the Alto's) to help out with torso ventilation.I tried my jacket out for a day before returning it. It looks much better than the Alto when worn but with the much better Mammut Ultimate Pro Jacket in my closet the Mammut Plano would NEVER get worn by me.Funny Note: Mammut puts a belay zipper on this jacket although the sleeves are not articulated. So climbers won't rush to pay $200+ for the Plano that they can't use comfortably. So the people that would buy and like the Plano (casual trekkers and city folk) would never need to use the belay zipper other than maybe ventilation around a backpack hip belt. Either way I don't get it.BOTTOM LINE: If the retail price was at $80 to $120 then I would gladly recommend the Plano for a someone looking for a casual stylish Mammut Jacket. The positives are Mammut does provide plenty of modern wearable colors all of which I love in the Plano to attract a wide range of buyers. However that recommendation I just made was a hypothetical on ONLY based on the price of the Plano being in the sub $100 range. However in reality, serious outdoors-folk and climbers would already know on their own to spend $200 elsewhere. For everyone else at the $200+ retail price the Plano touts I can NOT in my right mind and sound conscious recommend the Plano to anyone willing to spend that much on a soft shell. They are literally scores of much better, better priced jackets out there that would put the Plano and Mammut's entire marketing department to shame!"
summary: Great SOFtech revision to Alto! Mammut fixes fit but not comfort!

reviewText: This had to be the easiest to apply skin I've ever tried on any product. It's also cut properly, so it fits nicely into place without much effort. (I'm the kind of person who can go crazy with trying to center something if it's not the absolute right size.)It comes with a little spray bottle you use to moisten your fingers and both sides of the skin. This makes everything slick and nearly impossible to wreck with fingerprints. It doesn't stick to everything it touches, so you can quickly slip-slide it into place. It took me more time to get ready to use it than to actually use it. (Washing my hands, polishing the Droid's glass, washing my hands again, creating a dust-free location to work, washing my hands again... you get the idea.)At first, the residual liquid under the skin makes it look horrible. However, the instructions recommend leaving the phone turned off for 12-24 hours after applying the skin, so I did. I put the skin on in the early evening and left my phone off over night. After a few hours the liquid between the skin and the glass had dried enough to show promise. By the next morning, the skin had dried completely and the worst of the imperfections were gone. Today, three days later, there are still two tiny bubbles near the edge, but I expect they will be gone soon. (The instructions say it could take several days for the imperfections to work out completely.)The skin is not as smudge-prone as the plain glass, so I don't have to wipe it clean every time I touch it. It also adds a slightly-rubbery feel to the surface which actually makes the phone a little easier for me to use. That is, the touch screen doesn't seem quite so hair trigger responsive -- I can scroll more easily without accidentally clicking something I didn't mean to.I would recommend this skin to others, and if I need a skin for another gadget, this is the first company I will check.

I owned my original iPhone for two very happy years.  I wanted to upgrade to the 3GS but my husband and I agreed that it would be smart to switch to Sprint in order to save money.  Well, I wasn't very happy about this.  My husband has a Palm Pre, and he's all ga-ga over it, but I wanted a phone with a virtual keyboard, so I initally got the HTC Hero.  After two weeks I couldn't take it anymore... it was simply not easy to use and the virtual keyboard drove me nuts.  So I traded it in for a Palm Pre (to my husband's secret delight).I miss being part of the "iPhone club," having a bigger screen, and having virtual voicemail... but outside of that?  I'm a very happy customer.  The Palm Pre has turned this unwilling recipient into a proud owner.What do I like about it?  EASE OF USE.  The HTC Hero was a headache to understand.  With the Palm Pre, I was able to figure it out within a day or two, as though I had been using it for years.  The cards system of multitasking is genius in its simplicity, and very effective.  I can easily flow from the web browser to my emails to my texts and calendars effortlessly.It also helps that the Palm Pre is a much more open ecosystem than the iPhone, which allowed my husband to install an iPhone theme onto my Pre (for old-time's sake!), to make it look exactly like an iPhone.  I know you can "jailbreak" an iPhone to do this also but the vast majority of people don't know how to do that, whereas any average Joe can make the Pre look and sound just like a Pre.  My husband actually DESIGNED a Blackberry theme for the Pre and it's one of the most frequently downloaded.Another thing I really like about the Pre is the screen.  It's smaller, but vibrant and beautiful.  The HTC Hero had 65,000 colors, but the Palm Pre? Sixteen million!This may sound silly but another feature I like is the mirror on the back of the Pre's slider.  Ladies (and guys, you too!)... this is a very useful feature!Palm's App Catalog has a growing number of apps, some of which I find really useful, like Pandora, Google Maps, and Flixster.  I haven't missed the thousands of iPhone apps quite like I thought I would because to be honest I didn't download that many when I had my iPhone.I really like the camera on the Pre.  Fast shutter times, and great outdoor quality pictures.  Indoors the quality suffers in low light... but when there's NO light then we can use the Pre's built-in flash.Finally, updates. I like how Palm regularly updates this phone.  With the iPhone they would only come once in a while.  It's good to know that Palm is continually striving to improve their product.  The Pre now saves pictures and copies text from the browser and forwards text messages.  Full flash capability is coming soon which will make the browser even better.  (My husband told me to put that part in!)Things I don't like? Battery life is pretty bad.  My phone will certainly be dead in the morning if I forget to charge it overnight.  My husband surprised me with a Touchstone charger and if you get this phone you HAVE to get this accessory.  I don't have to fiddle with wires or anything... just set my phone down and I'm done.  Another thing I don't like is that things aren't quite as snappy on this phone as on my friend's iPhone 3GS... but it has gotten faster with updates and again I can do more than one thing at once on the Pre.That's pretty much it!  I'm not a very techie person, just an average consumer and smartphone user.  I thought I would miss the iPhone more than I am now, but to be honest, the Palm Pre has been a pleasant surprise.  I really like it.  If you're on Sprint or on another network considering the Pre, it gets my vote.
summary: Came from an iPhone with high expectations... and they were met!

After having the HTC Trophy for about a week, I believe it is a solid 4 stars and an improvement over the iPhone 3G I had.The Windows Phone operating system is really a pleasure to use - so many things are integrated into the tile system.  For example, without launching a single app, I can know the weather forecast, how my stocks are doing, see Facebook updates, and see details of any missed calls or texts.  Because the tiles have variability and animation, I often get "hey that's cool" comments from people only familiar with Android or iOS.I realize my iPhone 3G was getting old for a tech device, but there is a big performance gain with the Trophy.  Web pages load more quickly, Facebook no longer crashes, and the music player seems less buggy.  This could be a difference between the AT&T; network and Verizon, but for the purposes of this review I am mentioning it because other potential buyers could be in the same situation.Let's not forget that this is first and foremost a phone, and as a phone the Trophy does a good job - calls are clear, reception seems to be fine, and battery life for me has been lengthy (going over 2 days between charges).  The voice to text feature is phenomonal - saves me time and effort when I need to send a quick text and can't quite type safely.Why not 5 stars?  First, as everyone knows, the Marketplace for Windows Phone is not nearly as deep as that of the Apple App Store.  Want a coloring game for your toddler?  You are probably not going to find it for this phone.  Three apps I had that I can't find for the Trophy are Fidelity Investments, Chase, and Shredder Chess as examples.If you currently own Android or iOS and have a bunch of apps that you can't live without, I would look on the Windows Phone Markeplace and make sure they are there before switching - likely you'll want to stay where you are because the apps are paid for.  However, if you do not own a multitude of apps and want to try a much better phone and operating system, it is my opinion that you will not regret trying the HTC Trophy.  I switched and I'm very happy I did.
summary: Switched from iPhone to HTC Trophy

I have a few of these hard plastic Centro covers. They are attractive and protective.Note: I do not use the belt clip, so I have no idea if that works. Also, I typically have both a hard plastic cover AND a silicon skin on my Centro, to doubly protect it from my clumsiness and occasional dropping of my Centro!Features--Color: the actual color of this hard cover is much more pink and vibrant than the pink shown on Amazon.com. I would call it "HOT pink" or "HOT magenta" rather than "magenta." So that came as a bit of a surprise. However, it was not enough of a surprise or disappointment for me go through the hassle of returning it.Feel: This cover has a "matte" rubbery-type feel to it. This is nice, because it prevents your Centro from sliding off surfaces (such as your dashboard, your lap while you are driving, etc.) (Yes, I know, I know... no cell-phoning while driving... but let's be real, people do this all the time.)Durability: you can drop your Centro with this cover on, and it will be fine. (I have done this a few times with this cover on! However, to be fair, I also had a pink silicon skin on at the same time. So perhaps it was because of the silicon skin. I like my Centro protected well!)Keyboard, stylus, screen, camera, ports: This cover has holes for keyboard, stylus, screen, camera and syncing/charging ports. This means you can use all of these without the cover getting in the way.It also means if you want your screen or keyboard protected from scratches or spills, you'll have to buy separate screen/keyboard covers, or just buy a different skin/cover. I use screen protectors I bought separately.Third, the cover's easy to put on, but hard to take off. My job requires daily contact with sick people. So I like to take the cover off periodically, to completely disinfect the cover AND the Centro, to prevent carrying around MRSA or something.In the case of this (and all my other) hard plastic cover(s), it's hard to pry it off the Centro without either breaking the cover, or scratching your Centro. I cannot honestly give these a bad review. They are a great product, and are a fantastic value. Unfortunately, they do not adequately suit my family's needs.My girls tend to be tough on chargers and adapters. These have held up surprisingly well under their abuse, but we could still do better with tougher cables.My wife and I own Samsung's higher end Android offerings. Like many other folks, we experience extended charge times with these cables. When I had one go bad and cut the ends off it so it wouldn't get used accidentally, I realized the problem with my electrical training.In order to make these cables as flat as they are, the wires inside them are incredibly thin. In fact, about as thin as the wires in a telephone handset cord, possibly thinner. Our modern high powered devices require 1 to 2 amps output from the charger, some require more. The electrical current is carried only on the outside of the electrical conductor (this applies to all electrical circuits). This problem is compounded by the longer length of these cables. The longer a cable or wire is, the thicker it has to be in order to ensure that all of the necessary power reaches the end.Since the wire is so long and thin, physics dictates that it cannot carry all of the current to our devices. This means only a fraction of the power is getting to our devices. The result is long charge times, or devices that continue to lose charge in spite of being plugged in.If you are having charging issues, use heavier cables, just understand that you will have to pay substantially more for them.Neither the cables nor the seller deserve a bad review.

I'm a fan of the AmazonBasics brand. I've found quite a few of their products to be the equal or better of their counterparts, usually at a percentage of the price. When this case became available for review, I thought it would be an excellent time to take it for a spin on a new iPhone 5. After spending a month with it, and comparing it to the Belkin Grip Candy Case / Cover for New Apple iPhone 5 (Black / Ice), I feel confident about being able to compare this case against a name-brand competitor as well as judge it on its own merits.This case has two pieces. The cover that surrounds all but the face of the phone, and a thin film that protects the screen as well. The cover was very easy to install. It fit the iPhone 5 perfectly, and the side and top buttons were completely covered, with raised areas of the cover to indicate their location. Holes provide access to the mute switch, Lightning connector port, and speaker.The plastic material is a flexible vinyl-like material that looks nice while providing a little more grip to a phone that I found to be a little on the slippery side after spending 3 years with an iPhone 3GS. It's shiny without being cheap looking and it feels like it would provide some cushion in the event of a drop. (no iPhones were dropped in the course of preparing this review) That combination of grip and slip worked well for putting the phone in jeans pockets as well as coat chest-pockets. I never felt like it was in the way.The power and volume buttons are a little difficult to activate, however. I had hoped that this would improve with time, but it did not. I'm not the type to constantly fiddle with thos buttons, so it wasn't a big deal, but it's something to consider if you use those buttons often.Compared to the Belkin cover, the AmazonBasics cover isn't as nice. The Belkin looks nicer (although I would have preferred an all-black unit to the Belkin's bi-color scheme. The smoke color of this cover works well with the black phone.Up until now, I have not mentioned the screen cover, and that is because it is the weakest aspect of this cover. I've never had a screen protector before, so I can't compare it to others, but I found the cover difficult to apply without bubbles that I couldn't remove with the included card and small dust particles kept getting in between the screen and the sheet when I was installing it. I was also disappointed with the alignment of the holes in the protector, as they were off-center by about 1/8". I tried to lift the sheet after installing it so that I could remove some dust, and then that corner never applied itself as well again. This might all be user error, but I just removed it and threw it away. Kudos to Amazon for including a protector sheet, as the higher-priced Belkin cover did not.For the price, I think the AmazonBasics cover did its job. However, I think this is one of those situations where you do get what you pay for, and those looking for more will need to pay more than the economical price that this cover is currently being sold at. Covers are going to be a personal preference thing, so if the photos of this cover appeal to you, I can recommend it as well worth trying. At most, you'll have spent $10 and if you don't care for it you can pass it along to a friend or keep it around as a spare.
summary: Basic case that fulfills its mission but belies its price

I bought this phone specifically because it was one of the last "Smart" phones that came out before Verizon started requiring data plans on all smart phones. I just can't bring myself to pay $30/month for a data package when there is free wifi practically everwhere I go. As with all smartphones, it has it's quirks (hence the 4 star rating), but rebooting it once a week or so usually resolves any issues.I really like the slider keyboard. The buttons have a good feel to them and result in much less texting errors than a touch screen keyboard. I didn't think I would ever use the dialer buttons on the front, but I've found that I actually do use them quite a bit. Whenever I have to make a call to a number that is not in my contacts list, the buttons on the front are much easier to dial with than dialing on the touch screen.I also like that it comes with a stylus that conceals itself within the phone. Most of the things I do on the touch screen can be done with my fingertips, but sometimes the stylus comes in handy. I didn't really like the standard Windows Mobile user interface, so I installed SPB Mobile Shell, which makes this touch screen much more finger friendly. I also installed ThumbCal, which is a calendar app that is much better than the standard calendar. This phone can also open Word and Excel files, which I don't use very often, but the functionality is nice to have on board. I have the extended battery, and it will last for a full day, but if I do a lot of web surfing in a day then the battery will start to run out around 6 or 7pm. That's why I have a couple of spare batteries that I keep charged up, which I recommend.I know the days of smart phones without data plans are over, so I bought two of these so I can have another one when this one wears out. If you want a phone that has smart phone functionality, but not the smart phone monthly bill, definitely go with this one. You'll be glad you did, and you can take that $360/year you'll save and do something useful with it.
summary: A smart phone that has WiFi, and no data plan required!

I would pack two power strips and about 20lbs of chargers, setup a charging station in the hotel room and try not to forget anything when we checked out. Smartphone have replaced the MP3/DVD player and starting to replace PlayStation portable and Nintendo DS. The problem is that most smartphone take 700-800ma on the USB port to charge. Until the release of the iPad almost all USB chargers put out 5V@500ma or 2.5watts. With the 5W/10W charger I can charge three smartphone on one outlet. As a DJ and avid gamer I'm always in the market for new and decent quality headphones. I've owned and used many headsets over the years (a few SteelSeries) and there always seems to be something new for PC, gaming consoles, mobile devices and DJing.  As I always enjoy testing out new headphones here are my thoughts on the SteelSeries Flux In-Ear Pro Headset for Gaming and Music;Pros+ 3 different interchangeable ear tip sizes (1 set of foam ear tips are included as well) complete with a compact and convenient carrying case for everything.+ Earbuds fit snuggly in your ears (comes with a con see below)+ Mic/controller on cord allows for hands free calling and music control.  I tested it on myNokia Lumia 521 (T-Mobile)and it worked perfectly.+ Multi-platform use (PC, Mac and all mobile devices).+ Main length of cord is flat and very sturdy (some may view this as a Con).+ Decent noise isolation.Cons- High price point of $129.99.- Inserting them into your ears can be bothersome until you get the hang of it and beging doing it on a regular basis.  Also, if you wear glasses keeping the cords wrapped behind your ears can be troublesome.- Cord is a bit too short to be of practical use.  The main flat cable length is only 31 inches with the total length from earbuds to jacks being 52 inches.  This headset is meant to be worn wrapped behind the ears so you lose some length because of this design.- In ear headphones are not for everyone.  Many people experience discomfort while attempting to wear them.  I have very narrow ear canals so using the smallest ear tips is essential to avoid excess pressure.- Overall lackluster sound quality.Note: In order to maximize the sound quality of this headset it's extremely important to use the correct ear tip size and properly insert and position them in your ears.  Failure to do so will make these earbuds sound much worse than they really are.  The manufacturer instructions which are provided explain how to accomplish each of these things with clearly drawn diagrams.At the $130 range, the SteelSeries Flux In-Ear Pro Headset for Gaming and Music is sadly somewhat disappointing.  The audio quality is unfortunately rather lackluster with most music sounding hollow, flat and with very little bass.  Video games fared only slightly better with crisp and clear highs/mids but once again without any bass at all and dull sound overall.  I tried multiple more recent games (Borderlands 2, Bioshock Infinite, Dead Island Riptide) all resulting in the same distant sound.  I also used the headset with multiple tablets, mobile phones and portable gaming devices to listen to music and play games with little to no difference in sound quality.  Finally I thought I'd put them to the ultimate test in sound quality.  Good old fashion vinyl on the Technics 1200 turntables.  Here the headset shined a bit more, however I feel this was largely to due to the fact I was using a mixer which allowed me to individually adjust the bass, mid and high.  Using the headset for phone calls was nice and clear so they're easy to recommend for that purpose.  But the current asking price for the SteelSeries Flux In-Ear Pro Headset for Gaming and Music is just too much for what you're getting in my opinion.  If you're going to invest this kind of money and are willing to forgo the portability you're better off getting a good entry level over the ear set of headphones for all your gaming and music needs.
summary: All treble and no bass make this headset a dull buy (an honest review).

I bought the 2 TB version about 8 months ago to backup 6 PCs and 2 Intel NAS units in my small business. It is a nice package that runs quiet. I soon added 2 HDDs to get 4 TB w/ RAID. I would have made it 6 TB, but that would have required reconfiguring the original HDDs. Also , the two 1-Gbit ethernet ports apparently cannot both be used in the same LAN subnet, so I use only one.The BlackArmor Backup Software says Seagate v1.0 (always scary) but it is actually an Acronis product. Quite a few bugs. Credentials are an issue and the dialog where you must enter them is elusive. I used "Administrator" throughout rather than the default \\ComputerName\Administrator because how are you going to restore if ComputerName dies? There is a bug where if you edit a scheduled job and re-enter the password, it may concatenate the old and new passwords. Fortunately, if you reopen the dialog the black dots clue you that it has become twice as long and you can abort the edit. Otherwise, you could end up with a backup protected by "passwordpassword" and never figure out how to unlock it. Best to recreate the job rather than edit it. Today the backup software is still v1.0 with no bug fixes. The link for purchasing additional client licenses is as dead today as it was 8 months ago.I thought I could backup my Intel NAS units directly via USB, but no. I need to have a PC run the job, reading the NAS unit and writing to the Black Armor unit while making my LAN busy.I did eventually manage to define and schedule all my backup tasks and they have run reliably for 8 months. Today I had to completely restore a PC that got a virus and became unbootable. I had misplaced the BlackArmor CDROM. The relevant download page on Seagate website lacks a download link, still says v1.0, and states that you must email your download request along with hardware S/N. The support link is generic and you must log in. I got an email response 8 hrs later stating that "we do not currently offer email or chat support for our BlackArmor Network Storage Products" and offering an 800 number.  By then, I had located my CDROM and accomplished a near painless restore from a full system backup plus several monthly incrementals.Should this BlackArmor unit fail, can I read my Acronis backup files off the HDDs with another software product? I don't really know.I have copied files from the BlackArmor unit to Seagate FreeAgent Go via USB (for offsite backup) without involving PC or LAN. This browser-launched process does not use the Acronis software. I think that the BlackArmor unit is most suitable for use as working NAS with offsite backup to USB drive(s). Find a better software product to backup your PCs.
summary: Good hardware, poor backup software & support

reviewText: EDIT: Update - This product stopped working after less than a week of light use. Basically, the left channel of my stereo headset stopped working consistently unless I put pressure on the 3.5mm plug on the Shure product being reviewed. This can happen when a product is made with a cheap plug. Unfortunately, this is not something you can identify before purchase. I will not be buying anymore Shure headphones, and I may possibly avoid their legendary microphones because of this experience.As an HTC Incredible owner, I bought the Shure MPA-3C for iPhone on sale for $20, I'm not sure if I'd pay $40 for it, though build quality is solid. It does not come with headphones so you'll want to pair this with your choice of earphones that feature a short cord so the microphone hangs at an appropriate distance from your pie hole. I think some of the Shure headphones come packaged with this same model and this might be an alternative to some considering the Shure SE115m+(a 3 button iPhone compatible set with built in canal phones and microphone that apparently can be used with the Incredible, though reportedly the volume buttons don't work with the HTC).The MPA-3C has one button for everything. Call quality is very good - I have no complaints and my friend said she couldn't tell I was on a headset when I was driving with my windows up. I didn't have to hold the microphone up to my mouth, I just let it dangle.When a call comes in, 1 click will answer, 2 clicks will hang up, and holding the button down will send the call straight to voicemail which is nice.If you are on a call, 1 click will hang up.If your phone is idle, holding the button down opens the Voice Dialer, but you will have to look at and touch your phone to complete the command (i.e. "Call Voicemail").If you hold the Search button on your Incredible, the microphone will pick up your voice and work as expected.Here's how the MPA-3C works with the various HTC Incredible music player options:On all players listed below: 1 click will start/stop your music.Stock music player - 2 clicks will redial the last number called.Meridian Player(What I use): 2 clicks will forward the track(Nice!)For the following players, I have to disable headset controls on Meridian to get functionality:Pandora: 2 clicks will forward the track(Very nice since Pandora can be hit or miss).Last.fm and Slacker: No way to forward the track.Astro Player: Holding the button pauses the music and selects the next track. Click once more to play. (Odd, but it works well). I wasn't able to utilize Astro's voice commands.Xiialive: No functions work, including play and pause.

Returning this for a refund.************************************As an update to the above review based on the comments from all the " expert critics" out there.  I'm sorry if you don't uphold the same standards when it comes to image quality as I do as a professional photographer of over 20 years, but it seems that sadly that is the case with a lot of things today.  Folks are fine with accepting decent results, and even believing they are excellent, because the other options are of lesser quality.  If you're OK with A LOT of blurry photos combined with a loooooooooooooooong lag delay that makes it near impossible to capture that just right moment on a live subject then yes, this is the camera for you.  If like me, you expect the best results, and only give 5 star reviews when deserved, then stay away from this camera.  And no, as a professional photographer it did not take me over 1000 photos to figure out that I was getting blurry photos. I was very excited to finally have in-dash navigation and a backup camera, as well as a touch screen interface in my vehicle, so I chose the NX-602.  Overall, the unit's features are spectacular for the price, and the clean, simple Clarion look and previous experiences with high quality sold me.Upon receipt of the unit, I powered it up on a test stand on my desk so I could do all of the software updates.  This was a pretty detailed process, and if you're not very good on computers, may be impossible for you.  It requires a combination of USB memory sticks, micro and standard SD medial flip-flopping, multiple system restarts, a software interface on the computer, etc.  Seems life could have been easier by just simply burning a disk image to CD, inserting it in the unit, and having the NX-602 do the 30-step software updating process itself.  It took about 2-3 hours to do all of the updates--would have been longer if the unit was in the car.The user interface is fairly straightforward, but one drawback is that you cannot change the home screen icons--you're just stuck with what the programmers picked.  Also, this unit seems to be (unfortunately) plagued with bugs.  It freezes about every 2 times I turn my car off and back on.  On the USB music player (using a memory stick), it gets stuck on the "loading" screen indefinitely.  I've tried multiple sizes and brands of USB sticks with same results.  On the sat radio screen, sometimes you just can't select a channel on the touch screen until turn your car off and back on.  The touch screen works everywhere else but on the sat radio screen.  My biggest issue with this unit is the PROCESSOR SPEED.  It really couldn't be much worse.  It lags like you wouldn't believe.  That may be what all of the issues come down to--slow processor.  I would have paid an extra $200 for a processor that I didn't have to constantly wait a few seconds on every time I push a button.  Overall, I'm pretty disappointed with the unit, and 2 stars is generous.The GMOS interface was amazing and simple, and worked as designed.  Wiring was easy, the Clarion directions were great, and the unit looks awesome in the dash.  The extremely slow processor, and multiple software bugs almost make the unit inoperable.  If I can't get the bugs fixed after speaking with Clarion, I'll be returning it.

I purchased the 4TB version of this drive in March primarily for Time Machine back ups.  The Firewire is attached to my 2011 Mac Mini with 2011 iMac and 2011 Mac Air backing up via wireless.  Unlike some reviewers, I never had any mounting or partitioning issues with this drive running on Lion.  It worked flawlessly.  After doing the upgrade to ML last week, there was an issue with the drive showing up twice on the Time Machine back up disk selection screen.  Seemed to have gotten that resolved from going through the forums and it worked again for a few days, but now I am getting the same disk utility errors noted by other recent reviewers and have hit a brick wall.I read somewhere that if you run the disk utility from a prior OSX version on the Seagate, that will fix this particular problem, but of course I had already converted all my machines to ML by that point.  I am tired of messing with it and have enough redundancies with cloud drive back ups and drop box that I figure I can wait for either Apple or Seagate to sort out whatever the issue is.  However I would recommend staying away from purchasing this drive until such time especially if it is your only back up source.  I am giving it 3 stars as it did work for me as advertised out of the box and hopefully will soon again.  Then again, it really should just work regardless of operating system updates.  It is a Seagate hard drive for "Mac" afterall.UPDATE 8/14_______________________Being irritated leaving something technical unresolved, I decided to move the disk from the Mini and plug directly into the USB port on the Airport Extreme router.  Shut everything down (router, modem, computers) and restarted.  The whole point of using the Mini was for the somewhat faster data transfer rates offered by Firewire over USB 2.....long story short, Mini was able to find the disk and I left TM backing up over night.  Success.  Got the iMac and MBA backed up today.  So far so good.  Seems in my case the problem may have been Firewire related (not about to move the Seagate back to the Mini and test one of the USB ports there to prove it, though).  Perhaps some diabolical plot by Apple and Seagate to force the ditching of Firewire in favor of Thunderbolt cables and disk adapters.  Anyway, this was an expensive disk so I'm glad to have it working again and hope the above helps.  Will report back if anything changes.
summary: Worked fine until Mtn Lion upgrade (UPDATE)

The quality of this backpack is excellent.  The material is heavyweight with a very nice finish -- it's not the usual ballistic or cordura nylon, but rather a heavyweight fabric that almost looks like a grey flannel suit.  The stitching is even all around, and the zippers are high quality with oversize pulls.  The shoulder straps are wider than many packs of this type, with excellent padding.  The case has an insanely generous 25 year quality guarantee, which speaks to Case Logic's confidence in the quality.  It also has nice details, like velcro loops that wrap up excess webbing from the shoulder adjustment straps (this is very handy if you tend to hang the backpack from the hook on a rolling suitcase -- otherwise the straps tend to trail out and drag on the ground behind the pack).On the downside, the design -- and therefore usability -- of the case is not so great.  The straps are anchored in front of the laptop compartment, so you have to flip them around the front of the case to get at the laptop.  Not a big deal (and even a benefit if you're afraid someone will try to steal your laptop while the case is on your back), but it makes the laptop compartment more of a pain to use.  The main compartment has a "suitcase style" opening so that it zips all the way open and folds out flat.  That might be useful if you're using the backpack as a suitcase, but it isn't useful when carrying folders and notebooks.  The main compartment has a laptop sleeve stitched to the back wall, but given the position of the sleeve and the position of the main compartment zipper, it's more of a struggle than it need be to get a tablet in an out when the case is fully loaded.  The main compartment doesn't have any dividers -- OK for a camping pack, but a business/student pack would benefit from having them.  The gadgets pocket on the front similarly is mostly just an extra compartment -- it has has a couple of pockets stitched to the back, but mostly it's just a big pouch in which to throw stuff.  Personally, I like gadgets compartments with multiple compartments inside so that I don't have to dig through the pouch looking for things.  The "hidden" lumbar pouch is an interesting idea, but not a comfortable place to carry things if you're walking any distance.In a nutshell, for a business/student backpack, I prefer either a pack with more built-in compartments to keep things organized and make it easier to find (e.g., the Everki Flight Checkpoint Friendly Laptop Backpack), or one that offers maximum space and comfort (e.g., the Full Speed Shine Backpack).  The Case Logic Berkely Plus Backpack is very well built from high quality materials, but it doesn't have the ergonomics/comfort of packs like the Full Speed Shine or the inherent organization efficiency of packs like the Everki Flight.  I'm a long time fan of Case Logic's disc storage products, and the quality of this backpack doesn't disappoint, but its design isn't what I was hoping for, and it will become my backup backpack, not one I use every day.
summary: Excellent construction quality ... not great design
