You should know that Netgear does not sell this modem to individuals, only ISPs.  At least that's what Netgear keeps telling me.  It's pretty frightening when a company that is supposed to be a major internet player can't do a Google search to see that over 100 stores sell this modem directly to users.My CMD31T died six weeks after it was purchased.  One day it was working fine and the next day I had no internet connection with my ISP.  First I called my ISP and did all the stuff they asked.  Then my ISP sent out a technician with a network analyzer.  My connection was fine, the modem was not.  Then the nightmare begins.The Netgear support number connects to a call center in India.  Everyone there follows the script EXACTLY. The first Customer Service Representative (CSR) told me that Netgear does not do support for this modem, I have to call my ISP.  I call my ISP to check and they confirmed that since this was a privately purchased modem that Netgear was responsible for support. The second CSR had me do a bunch of diagnostic steps.  Nothing worked, but since I could still see the GUI in the modem, the modem MUST be fine.  The third CSR told me to call the ISP and when I asked to speak to a supervisor, blew me off.  The forth CSR said someone from Netgear would call me. I'm still waiting for an RMA so I can return this modem two weeks later.BTW, forget any support if you run Linux.  You can tell the CSR your IP address, DNS, and default route, (which are MUCH easier to find in Linux) but if you are not running windoze they tell you they can't do support.The technician from the ISP recommended Arris or Motorola.  I bought a Motorola modem because I might not ever get an RMA from Netgear.If you buy this modem and it fails you will not get any support from Netgear.9 March 2012 Update:My first Email contact with Netgear was 22 February 2012. I have sent them my Amazon purchase receipt twice.  Still no RMA from Netgear.  I am sending an Email to Netgear Technical Support every few days telling them I still have not received an RMA.  If I ever receive an RMA I will post how long it took.So far my Motorola SURFboard SBG901 is working O.K.  It's not DOCSIS 3.0 but at least it works.22 March 2012 Update:It looks like Netgear is never going to send me an RMA. The only response I get from Chithra or Vishnu or Simbhu or Arif is "Please wait so that they can get the necessary details from them to assist you better."  I will be happy to post or forward any of these Emails from Netgear.Netgear automatically closes any support case in seven days if you do not reply to their Email.  They are hoping I will get tired of waiting and just write off the $90 I paid for the CMD31T.  Please think twice before buying any Netgear product24 March 2012 Update;Check out the comment from Netgear!!!  They won't respond to my support case but they sure as heckfire will try and spin bad PR!!!  Oh, IPV6 is the problem?  Then why has my Motorola modem worked perfectly the day after my Netgear modem failed? Maybe Motorola makes a better product than Netgear.  Or maybe my ISP temporarily switched to IPV6 and then waited until I called to tell them I bought a Motorola modem and immediately switched back to IPV4 so the Motorola modem worked.  Hmmm...  I wonder?

This system is mediocre, admittedly. It is a low end system price wise. I needed a halfway decent surveillance system in a hurry and on a tight budget, so this appeared to be an ok deal at Sams Club for 350ish. Setting up was easy enough, the dvr's menus are fairly easy (if somewhat clunky) to navigate. I have not set it up on the network but it should be doable (I'm a sysadm by trade.)Biggest gripe so far is, I had one bad camera out of 8, sent it in to replace, they sent it back NOT FIXED. Problem was the sensor making the image completely white in full daylight. Obviously it was not tested in daylight, so I made the company pay return shipping since I already paid the first time when they did not fix it. In the meantime, I purchased one camera from Home Depot to replace the broken camera. Guess what, THAT cam had the same problem - actually you can see where the sensor was glued wrong and doesn't even sit in the small window where the light comes in - so the stupid camera is in night-vision mode all the time (just like the original camera.)So, here I am still waiting for a working camera, after a month.  Defender's tech support is really slow, but I guess I can't complain too much being it was so cheap.As far as image quality - it's not great. You can change the resolution but even with the mode set to D1 (highest resolution/lower frame rate) you get pretty choppy blocky images. It should be sufficient for most purposes, and it can be useful to identify perps, but I would not rely on it 100% as it's not gonna produce 1600x1200 resolution like a digital camcorder!The setup for framerate is confusing, the documentation is very lacking here. I had to find info elsewhere, and found this useful page on cctvforum under the subgroups:CCTV Forum > Digital Video Systems > Digital Video Recorders -> topic: Frame vs CIF[...][...]you will have to decide which you prefer: a higher quality picture at a lower frame rate or more frames per second with a lower quality picture. That's not uncommon. The typical high-quality recording is at 4CIF (704x480 in the U.S.) that is four times the resolution of CIF (352x240). Many DVR's can not do 4CIF at full frame rate (704x480@30fps.), so something has to give.[...]That page also points to a pdf manual for another cctv system that has much better explanations of CIF, resolution and frame rate. Wikipedia also has a page on CIF.Another problem I had was that the unit claims it's files are saved in h264 format, but, these files are headerless, so they are pretty much useless without the proprietary Windows utils to view or convert the files into a useable format (avi). Which could be a problem for non-windows users like me.Fortunately the programs did work in WINE on my linux system. Still, I would have preferred a useable format, the fact that the sales pitch touted H264 is one of the reasons I bought it - I also read that the DVR is a linux box under the hood, which was another selling point for me.I have other minor gripes, but not worth detailing really. If I need higher resolutions, I can upgrade the cameras to something better (I have a Sony cctv bullet camera somewhere, if I ever feel like digging it out of storage. It's only a B&W; camera with no night vision, but it has a zoom lens and much better imaging capabilities.) There are  much better cameras available (from other brand names), and this unit will control ONE pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) camera so that's a plus.Overall, it's an ok system for the price I paid. It's not worth more than half the MSRP.PS: I purchased a decent UPS to keep the system powered up during blackouts - or in case my cat-killing neighbor (reason why I installed surveillance in the first place) decides to shut off my power [power circuit box is outside.]I bought a Cyberpower 1500va / 900w unit, which stated it has two 8.5Ah batteries (but does not say if they're connected in parallel or in series - which would mean the difference between having 17Ah total power, or having 24 volts and 8.5Ah) - I am assuming they're in series which would give a total of 8.5Ah. The dvr consumes 1.5amps, the cameras consume (guestimating) 3 amps (there are 2 power supplies, I can't see the backs to get the actual amperage.) So, let's say a total of 5 amps to power everything, that would give me approx 1.5 hours on the UPS (the UPS reports 86 minutes, estimated. This also leads me to believe the batteries are connected in series.) That should be sufficient to see me through most power crises :)

reviewText: I picked up this unit from a local store for 50% off shortly after Christmas. NOTE: The unit does not come with any floss sugar.I tried making cotton candy for the very first time yesterday (1/21/2013) and was pleasantly surprised that it works.Some lesson learned:1. Cotton candy making should be done OUTDOOR not INDOOR!!  I tried making it indoor first and it was a HUGE mistake.  The floss sugar would spray all over the place like a sprinkler gone wild.  What a mess to clean up.2. It takes 10 minutes to warm up the machine the very first time and about 2 minutes afterwards before the floss sugar will begin building the web.3. DO NOT alternate floss sugar flavors or else the result will look and taste quite unpleasant.  I tried pink vanilla and then blue raspberry...yuck!!  Stick to one flavor.4. After each attempt, I find a buildup of melted sugar crystals around the plastic barrier piece. You have to remove the plastic barrier and clean out the sugar crystals or else your next attempt at making cotton candy won't be as successful.5. ONE tablespoon of floss sugar will result in roughly 4-5 inch diameter of cotton candy on a paper cone.Overall, the machine does what it says.  Built quality is quite cheap, but like I said...at 50% off, it was the best bang for my buck.

I have owned one of these units for anout 9 months.  During that time I have primarily used it as a closed grill for steaks, pork chops, burgers, and pannini.  It has worked very well and is easy to clean because of the removable grill plates with a nonstick surface.  I have been happy with it and now that we live in a condo that does not allow the use of outside grills, I use it more frequently.I recently had a problem with the unit.  I put a steak in it and for some reason decided to "help" it make contact with the steak by pressing down on the handle.  I didn't think much of this as it is advertised as a "press".  I was alarmed when I heard a loud POP and watched a blue flame shoot out the right side of the unit.  In the process I operated a circuit breaker.  In subsequent testing I found that the top plate no longer heated up indicating a likely open circuit due to the short circuit that I created by pressing down too hard.Afterwards, I reread the operating manual.  It mentions that, when making pannini, one should press down "lightly" on the handle.  I certainly must have exceeded lightly when I damaged the unit.  Because there is no warning in the operating instructions about this, I suggest this to be a possible defect and safety hazard, especially as the subjective instruction to press down lightly means different things to different people.  Obviously, I am in the heavy-handed category.I have since purchased another unit because it is otherwise well-conceived and functional.  One could probably design the unit with more protection against a heavy press.  I will be much more cautious in the future.Other minor issues are that the nonstick coating is not as slick nor as robust as it might be.  After 15 or 20 cleanings, I noticed some metal peeking through and cooking residue does not always just float away without some rubbing.  The top plate is a little tricky to put back in as gravity fights against you when the lid is in the open position.  If you open the lid all the way to a flat position, it is easier. The top and bottom plates are labeled as such but the label is embossed in the metal plate and you have to look closely to see it.  The top and bottom plates are not interchangeable.  The lid is hinged so that it can adjust to the thickness of the food when closed and still be parallel.  The operation of closing the lid over food can be tricky as it doesn't always self adjust and may push the food out the front when closed.  You can avoid this by reaching to the back of the top and guiding into parallel position.  This must be done with heatproof gloves on because the top gets very hot.

The worst part is that after carefully following instructions, some pieces of the unit have gaps (upon close inspection) and the doors don't align on the unit and have to be carefully jiggled to close properly.This unit is a piece of junk and is not worth the $142.00. At best it's worth $70.00 but knowing what I know now, I wouldn't buy it for any price.Updates:*6/7/2012: I have had this item assembled for less than a week and the hinges on one of the doors have already broken.*8/12/2012: a side piece on the bottom of the unit has broken off after attempting to slide the unit an inch on my carpet with nothing heavy on top or inside of the unit.

I purchased the Total Chef Oven in February, 2004. We were very pleased with it cooking performance. However, within a month, the heating elements didn't work. It cost me $20.00 to ship the part back to Koolatron and we received the repaired unit within a month. Shortly after this, we started noticing cracks in the plastic dome, small at first but continually getting larger and more numerous. It now has pieces breaking off and is totally unuseable. This is not and was not the result of dropping it or any misuse on our part. After spending 20 minutes trying to get through to Koolatron, they refused to honor their warranty, though it clearly states that the dome is covered up to a year from date of purchase. I asked to speak to a supervisor, but was told one was not in the building and I would be called within 24 hours. Needless to say, no one has bothered. For your own sake, don't waste your hard earned money on this poorly produced product by this unethical company.

While small and maneuverable, this vacuum is not easy to use and does not vacuum on carpet well. The buttons are poorly designed and get stuck frequently; the roller bar frequently jams. In order to use the detachable hose, the vacuum must be in its relaxed position which makes it very difficult to carry upstairs. I have had my vacuum for three years and have never been impressed with its suction ability. This morning, while vacuuming, my dyson began spitting out dust instead of sucking up dust and quit working. Since it's Sunday I cannot get a hold of anyone (which is fine - it's Sunday) but now I have a streak of dust that my vacuum cleaner shot out and I cannot clean it because the vacuum quit working. It's only been three years!

Tried various types of grounded coffee and this product would not allow the water to appropriately drip/filter through coffee. End product was watered-down coffee. Disappointing considering these plastic filters were not cheap.

Seriously - I've purchased a million things on Amazon and this product was by far the worst. You could scald yourself just trying to open the overly stiff spout, let alone trying to remove the lid, which feels like it was hammered into place. This product should be RECALLED! If you value your skin and the skin of your loved ones, don't buy this product!  Le Creuset should be ashamed of themselves for putting this thing on the market, and Amazon should be ashamed for listing it.  By the way, I wouldn't have given this thing any stars if I wasn't required to in order to submit this review.
summary: Worst tea kettle ever!  And dangerous!

i think the design on the blanket is tight, but its too thin. i mean when you say fleece im thinking its going be all warm but its not. i have to use another blanket on top of it to stay warm

I purchased this coffeemaker because it had all the features that I want--programmable, thermal carafe, no filter.  It has a great price point and makes good coffee. I like the choice of coffee strength--regular, bold and robust.I noticed early on that the plastic is of lower quality than my previous coffeemakers (Capresso).  This results in a lot of condensation on the base and the carafe.  At first, this was just an annoyance.  But within 3 months, I noted that the warmer plate began rusting.  Now, after less than four months, the entire plate has peeled and is one big rusty plate.I have called to replace it under warranty.  At first, I was instructed to cut off the cord, take a picture of the disabled unit, pay $14.99 for shipping, and a new unit would be sent.  After objecting to disabling the first unit prior to receiving the second (how would I then make coffee?), I was "allowed" to pay for shipping with the promise of disabling the unit after I received the replacement, or else my warranty would be voided.  I would also like to mention that the HB representative seemed a little put out with my request, despite the fact it was I who paid money for the faulty unit from the start.  By the way, I paid for the shipping over the phone with a credit card (another source of annoyance to HB--I didn't want to give my credit card number when she called me from an anonymous 800 number), and, after a month, I have no replacement coffeemaker.
summary: Rusty warmer plate, poor customer service

reviewText: This pan is a piece of junk, I don't understand or believe it's possible for anyone to give this pan 1 star never mind 5. when it gets hot it warps out of shape with the food on it. After all the research I tried to do before purchasing a thermos, I still haven't found what I'm looking for.  This thermos arrived and I quickly unpacked it, recycled the packaging, hand-washed it, and left it to dry for use the next morning...  I brewed my tea and watched the garbage truck come and go. Utter garbage, a waste of resources, and I'm not sure I can even recycle it.

I am sorry, i do not know if the towel that I received was different than all the five star ratings but this towel was as thin as a paper towel  so i am sending it back-it doesn't feel good, it is thin and really  like no other towel that i have ever purchased-there is no terry looping to it at all-it is very, very flat without the plushness that i was looking for--you know the towels  in better hotel rooms, the ones that are plush and fluffy and just great feeling??? I loved the design of this timer; it was so simple, both easy to use and to see.  The alarm was also a good balance between being loud enough to hear but not ear piercing.  I'd had it for about a month when the magnet fell off.  My husband was able to fix that, though it was disappointing that it happened so soon.Today, the timer simply died.  It started turning itself off and on at random.  I watched it for a while to make sure I wasn't going crazy.  It really did turn itself back on and would turn off when it was ready, not when I pushed the stop button. I placed the order on 18 January, so I've had this timer for less than two months and the thing is ready for the trash heap!  We use timers often around the house, and this is by far the shortest lived one I've had.
summary: Big Disappointment - Dead in Under 2 Months

reviewText: We knew it would take weeks for the stools to ship. After easy assembly, 2 of the 4 stools kept falling apart. The screws wouldn't stay in and the wood cross bars didn't fit properly. Emailed seller, they said they would ship out new legs for both stools. Waited weeks again, never got them! Online I put in for a full refund. That evening they called, said they had no idea we were waiting for a shipment. Once again, they said they will send replacement legs. We did get the legs this time. I had high hopes for these sheets as they were 600 thread count for a good price - I guess you get what you pay for!  I owned them for only a week and very quickly returned them to Amazon - after they were washed I could not get the wrinkles out - I followed the recommendations and even ironed them - all to no avail.  I would highly suggest that you do not waste your time or money buying them unless you like the wrinkled, dishevelled look.  I would give these sheets no stars if I could!

reviewText: This machine is really cool.  It cuts and chops exactly as advertised.  It makes super quick work of a potato and is really well designed.  It is super easy to clean and a lot of fun to use.  However,  the fourth or fifth time we pulled it out of the box to use it, it broke. It has a one year warranty that doesn't seem to cover anything, especially the shipping which makes the warranty useless when it would cost more to ship the broken item than to just buy a new one.

I decided to wipe up the water with a paper towel and guess what.... it was dirty water! You are pretty much just pushing around dirty water on your floors. reviewText: Although this has a nice look to it, I didn't get what I expected. The spring was not strong at all, it has to be almost completely depressed to have any strength, meaning that you have to have a perfect fit for the height of the rods. It comes with a top and bottom rod, 3 full size middle rods and 1 half size middle rod. In order to make this fit top to bottom the rods will need to be with in 6 inches of the height of your desired placement while fully depressed. If you stack this with more than 3 shampoo bottles as seen in the picture, the weight will push the spring down and it will fall over, so you'd better have a good and tight fit, which means again that you need to have the spring almost fully depressed. If the spring was stronger this might be worth the money. Don't buy, good idea, bad design.

I have purchased this rug after reading reviews. The color of the rug was lighter than shown in the picture, but I did not want to bother with it. After shedding off about half of its softness in the washer, it continued shed in the dryer...  The only thing I do like about it is it's lenght. Over all I am disapointed with this purchase.

I must say that I totally disagree with universalradio. I am sorry to see how many people were swayed by that review. I, too, have owned and used almost every day for months both the Jack LaLanne Power Juicer and the Juiceman Jr. I have the opposite opinion of the two juicers. I had to leave behind my Power Juicer when I moved, so replaced it with the Juiceman Jr. What a mistake!!! The Juiceman Jr. is so inferior to the Power Juicer! reviewText: This is kind of a neat little gadget. It can take veggies and make them fun and pretty all at the same time. It cuts the hard vegetables into these wavy thin slices like noodles and can be cooked so many different ways. It is a manual device so no batteries or cords are needed and can be used anytime and be stored in a drawer. It comes with a little bottle type of cleaning brush to help keep it clean. It is fairly easy to clean too. You take any hard vegetable and insert it into one end or the other and turn like you were gong to sharpen your pencil. This product does work but for me did take a lot of practice to get the curls. But once I got sort of the hang of it, I did manage to get a lot of strips of vegetables for my salad. I have to admit it made a pretty salad. Some of you may be better at using this product than I, but I think just about anyone can eventually get and use it will pretty good success. Would I recommend this product? Well if you want a fancy looking salad or veggies and are willing to practice until you can do it, Then yes, but just on a general bases I have to say no for me. I do not do that many fancy things in the kitchen. Will I use it again since I have one? Well yes I will still use it when I want the look of a fancy dish or just thin cut vegetables.
summary: On the fence about this one...

I have tried using just plain fruit and yes, that isn't bad.  But  it seems like a lot of fruit gets stuck inside the machine too.  I use my Nutri Bullet instead to blend frozen cubes of coconut or almond milk, frozen berries and a banana ... and though it is not an ice cream texture (more like a thicker shake), this tastes AWESOME.  And it's just easy to clean and make.  Bottom line for me: Yonanas is too much work to make this so-called ice cream and the end result is not worth it.  I wish I could return this and just get a real ice cream maker instead.  If you buy it, keep your expectations low and you might be happy!

I talked to Sears who did try to fix it without luck but they would not return the vac either and actually, they shouldn't have to - it isn't their fault. This was purchased through a 3rd party seller who seemed to be honest and reliable. I even went to their website and read all of the glowing reviews (which I now KNOW for a FACT are completely fabricated) and boasts of exceptional customer service. What a joke! This hose is very, very poorly made:1) The hose is constructed from an extremely thin plastic. With minimal movement, it twists upon itself and kinks, completely cutting off suction. It is more prone to kinks than imaginable. I can hardly get a few feet without a kink.2) The hose texture is rough and beats the heck out of everything it brushes against. It is also very loud as it moves across the floor. (I am STILL waiting for my exorbitantly priced sock cover to arrive, if it ever does)3) The white color leaves marks on furniture legs and edges with MINIMAL contact.4) It doesn't easily swivel at the handle, making it very prone to looping which leads to those dreaded "kinks" I mentioned earlier. I have to stop every few turns and unwind the hose.5) The handle is at an odd angle and requires a wrist-twisting position to get it to vacuum well. This makes it very fatiguing and eventually painful to use.6) The button-lock mechanism is flimsy so that the button on the handle doesn't fully "lock" with the attachments.  During use, the attachments either fall off or get jammed on so tight, they are very difficult to remove.7) MY BIGGEST COMPLAINT and the reason I contacted the company is due to the suction control ring on the handle. What a joke! A serious design flaw complicated by cheap materials. The C-shaped piece of plastic that covers the suction hole and enables suction control does not stay in the "grooves" of the handle. Not only does it not stay where you position it for suction control, it literally slides up and down the handle of the hose. The SECOND time I used this crappy hose (and I am very gentle with everything I own), the ring slipped off of the vacuum and is gone. (Most likely behind or under a very large piece of furniture- after weeks of searching, I have yet to find it). I now use a piece of tape over the hole to control the suction. How nice is that for a BRAND NEW hose! If I was going for the taped-up hose look, I would have kept the old hose that had tape covering the crack it got from years of use.When I contacted the company (it has an M and a D in the name), I got ZERO response. After two emails and multiple calls, I decided to write an honest product review on their website. Believe it or not, I was not able to post my review. Apparently, the company ONLY posts positive reviews. How is THAT for honesty!Don't waste your money on this piece of trash! Spend a little more and buy an original/factory replacement hose. This product is WAY overpriced and will give you nothing but grief and frustration.

Probably due to it's "electro-static" feature, the thing is a dust magnet...you can clean it thoroughly, place it in a clean spot, and the following day the entire machine is evenly coated with dust. Worst of all, it frequently decides to spray dirt and dust all over the place, creaing a FAR bigger mess than the one you're attempting to clean up!I'd give it 0 stars if I could.  Or negative stars, seeing as how it's better suited to creating messes than cleaning them. Whomever designed this steaming pile should be fired.  Or imprisoned.I just bought a Dyson DC25.  It's expensive, but works like a dream.  If you want my Eureka, it will be sitting out at the curb next Thursday morning!
summary: Horrible piece of junk, avoid at all cost!

I bought one of these because I figured it would be easy to dispense all of the water I wanted, and the large size would help me not need to fill the pitcher all the time. The water was decently filtered and the dispenser operated smoothly.The real problem I had with it was how much of a hassle I always found it to fill.  The jug dispenser was too large to easily fit in my sink, so I couldn't fill it up that way.  So I tried switching to a system of filling it up with consecutive glasses of water, but that was hard to do in the confines of my refrigerator.  I would end up taking the whole thing out of the fridge, filling it up with a number of glasses of water then trying to move the dispenser with the top half full back into my fridge without spilling it.  This really turned out to be too big of a hassle for me so the darn thing was always empty. I just went back to ye-old-fashioned pitcher and have never been happier.

If you want something that is going to grind coffee beans into something you can put into your coffee maker then this grinder is a gem since it is a decent quality machine that works reliably.If you really like drinking coffee, know the use of all of the grind settings on your local grocery store grinder, and you are going to compare your home grinder to that commercial grinder, then think twice before making this purchase.The fine grind setting on this machine generally produces a medium drip coffee grind.  The grind is somewhat variable so I've been a seeing a wide variety in the sizes in my grounds. The commercial machine at the store is very consistant.One downside of the time-grind function that many of these grinders have is that you can't really stop the grinder if output container fills up before the time stops.  Not only does that strain the motor but it also really compresses the finer grounds into hard clumps that you will want to break up before scooping.This may sounds like whining but what it boils down to is this:  a machine at this price point is not going to be able to compete with a commercial grinder.If you want the flexibility of occassionally grinding beans in your home, want a small inexpensive unit, and are not a perfectionist then you can get quite a bit of value out of this grinder.
summary: It's OK, if you don't expect commercial grinder results

As it is, you can only fold it over twice to close it. It isn't bad, but rolling would make it tighter to hold the knives. That is what is it is supposed to be. You are supposed to roll it and tie it tight so the knives and held together tight and so they aren't loose to bounce around and are protected from damage against hitting something else or being dropped.Also, because the velcro is really short, if you try to roll it tight, the velcro overshoots its target and you can't close it off. They should have either extended the velcro fuzzy side or used some other strap securing mechanism. This would have added a nickel to the cost I think.Overall, if you need something to contain your knives and don't want to spend much for a really good one, this will do the job. But it isn't anything special. It does look clean and neat though.

I was suspicious of this product's poor design from the beginning.- The water tank has a round top, so it won't sit by itself in a sink or bathtub while you fill it: you have to hold it steady. What was Honeywell thinking?- There are at least six different controls & a multi-display LED. All a humidifier really needs is a humidistat control and a temperature/fan speed control. Anything more is overkill and just something else to break in operation. After all, were talking about operating a humidifier here, not the starship Enterprise.- Way too many complicated parts. Again, evaporating water is pretty simple. In a pinch, you can do it with a pot on your kitchen stove. It shouldn't take a complicated machine to do the job. The mechanical complexity of the unit ultimately turned out to be its downfall.I bought the unit despite misgivings because it was rated highly by Consumer Reports, but of course they can't really test for long-term reliability. In my case, even short-term reliability turned out to be a problem. The unit water-feed started malfunctioning about a week after I bought it and put it in service. About 30 minutes after filling the tank, the well in the base of the unit would fill up and overflow. Disassembly and cleaning according to the manual did not fix the problem, nor was product support, so I eventually gave up and returned the unit. The one bright spot here was Amazon: they accepted the return with no questions asked, so I promptly bought a Vornado that I'm very happy with, again from Amazon.

17 months old and there was ice forming on the freezer floor and water leaking onto the kitchen floor. Even though it was a holiday weekend I was given a service appointment for the next day, a Saturday. $208 later, I was encouraged to buy a 3 yr service contract for $200. 6 days later the freezer worked fine but the refrigerator wasn't keeping cold. Nothing helped: turning the temp control all the way up and turning the fridge off and on again got no results. I felt angry that I'd obviously bought a bad fridge, but pleased that I purchased a 3 yr service agreement. Until I called for service. When I was told the next available appointment was 18 days away I hung up in disbelief, called back from a different phone and said I didn't have a service agreement. I was given the next available appointment which was in two days. During that time the refrigerator randomly started working again.The repairman called to say he was on his way. He said the charge for his visit would be a minimum of $100. When I told him I had a service agreement, he said he'd call me back. He didn't. I called him back - twice (caller ID is so handy). He finally arrived end of day, took the temp in the freezer and in the fridge and told me everything's fine. When I told him the refrigerator had stopped working for over 48 hours causing the temp to rise to 62 degrees, he told me next time it happens to just reboot by turning the circuit breaker off and back on. Like a computer. A computer? Really? I don't keep all my food and my prescription medication in my computer. And while having to reboot my computer might be annoying, it won't make me physically ill.Whirlpool is not at all interested in me or my Whirlpool refrigerator's problems. Customer service told me to call their authorized service repair company and then asked me, "Is there anything else we can help you with today?" When I told them about the fraudulent behavior their authorized service repair company engages in, they said they were sorry to hear about that but they couldn't help me.

I, unfortunately, bought this frother before checking any reviews. Got it on sale along with a Keurig coffee maker. By week 5, nada. Oh some bubbles in the milk, but no froth to spoon out. Thank goodness I saved my receipt and took it back today for a refund. How can a manufacture sell something that has such a shockingly high failure rate? It's pitiful, really. I am further shocked by how many reviews on all brands of electric frothers say those products break down after X amount of time. I just read tonight that you can make froth in a small French press coffee maker with a few pumps, or buy a manual frother (for about $25); which has a beaker, lid with pump. I did just try making froth in my French press. I heated some milk in the microwave, poured it into the French press and after 5-6 pumps, I had some nice froth. So it lasted about 35 days, sometimes using it a couple times per day.

I purchased my original Vue from BB&B; online and immediately had a problem with the "two streams" from the brew head (see this video posted by another purchaser: go to YouTube and search for "Keurig Vue Problem"). Each time I got the second stream of clear water in addition to the coffee stream, the coffee produced was very weak. (I should note that I have never used a powdered or milk style V-cup in the machine. I only use the standard ground coffee V-cups.) As this problem was causing me to waste a lot of coffee, I contacted Keurig for assistance. They had me run three water-only cycles through the system to "calibrate it" and the next cup I produced was perfect (only a single coffee stream from the front hole in the brew head). Unfortunately, the problem returned almost immediately and, once again, more than half of my subsequent brewing attempts were plagued by the "two streams" problem. I tried rinsing the brew head before each cup and running more water-only cycles, but nothing helped. I finally called Keurig again and they sent me a brand new replacement brewer. This one was only slightly better. I frequently still experienced the "two streams" problem. I believe the second hole (where the clear water exits) is not only designed for water-only cycles, but also to catch any owerflow from a standard brewing cycle. I think what is happening is that the upper (center) piercing unit is not sealing properly and the leakage from the poor seal is what is causing the second stream of clear water. In looking at a used V-cup, I can see a deep indentation in the foil lid between the center piercing and the lower piercing. My hunch is that the foil is not stiff enough to make a good seal between the piercing units at least part of the time. After using the replacement brewer for about two weeks with little success, I contacted Keurig support again and informed them of my continuing problem. I did note to them that I was in a high-altitude area (around 6000 ft) and that I had tried pre-piercing the center of the V-cup and it didn't help. Keurig support did state that they are aware of the "two streams" issue and that replacing the brewer has usually solved the problem. They recommended that I lower the brew temp to 187 degrees and try again. I did so without success. So I called Keurig support back and the rep stated that she would consult with their engineering department and call me back. I heard back from Keurig the next day and was told, per their Engineering Department, the "two streams" problem will occur at high altitudes (6000+ feet) due to low ambient pressure. Further, there is NO FIX for this issue. As such, I had to return my Vue brewer.I have posted my experiences here, at BB&B; and on another message board to inform prospective purchasers who live in higher altitude areas NOT to purchase the Vue so they can avoid the problems I have experienced.I am giving the Vue two stars because of Keurig's excellent customer service (even though they could not resolve my issue). Also, on the occasions when the Vue worked properly for me, it produced great coffee.5/16/12 Update:After reading posts here and elsewhere from people with similar problems, I decided to purchase another V700 (my third) and give it one more try. I set up the new unit and immediately started pre-piercing the V-packs in the center with a push-pin and flattening the foil prior to brewing. Using this technique, I have not experienced a single "two stream" problem with the new unit! I did try to brew a V-pack without piercing it and it worked much better than my earlier units, but did leak a few drops of clear water through the second hole in the brew head.I tried pre-piercing the V-packs with my earlier units, but I used a pocket knife to make a small slit in the center rather than the pinpoint hole made by the push-pin. I also did not flatten out the foil.With or without pre-piercing, this new machine functions much better than my earlier ones. I still believe that my altitude is a factor, but it pertains to the pressurized V-packs and not the "low ambient pressure" not allowing the machine to function properly as told to me by Keurig Engineering.To sum it up, I believe Keurig does have a hardware problem with some new V700 units - my current unit brews much better than my first two which were returned. That, combined with the pre-piercing technique described above, has allowed me to enjoy the latest Keuring technology despite my altitude and I will be keeping my new V700. I am not changing my original rating at this time due to the difficulties I experienced prior to getting a working setup. (I will provide another update if anything changes.)To those in high-altitude areas: I would now recommend that you try the new Vue, but be sure to purchase it from a vendor with a good return policy. If you are fortunate enough to get a good unit on the first try and use the technique described above, you will enjoy an excellent machine that produces quality beverages.
summary: 5/16/12 UPDATE: Keurig Vue may not function properly in higher altitude areas!

reviewText: SECOND UPDATE: My pan is mostly back to its old self. Going back to non-stick from horrendously sticky was actually quite simple, once I discovered the process.STEP 1: Wash pan as you would normally.STEP 2:Sprinkle inside of the pan liberally with baking soda. Not a ton, but a good coating you could push around with your finger.STEP 3: Spritz soda with a spray bottle filled with 1:3 vinegar and water, enough to saturate the baking soda completely. We're looking for a good bubbly reaction taking place here. I think it's the bubbles that do the job.STEP 4: After vinegar and soda have finished bubbling, wipe out and rinse your pan and look for any remaining residue. After trying this there was very little stickiness left in the pan. Only one or two small spots that continued to stubbornly stick, but I haven't retried this method either.I am curious to know how this works for other people, so if anyone tries it, please let me know!I used distilled white vinegar which I normally use for cleaning. I don't know exactly what happened, but this a process I started using on stubborn spots on my ceramic cook top stove with decent success, so I tried on the fry pan. The process seems to have restored the pan to it's lovely non-stick self.FIRST UPDATE:When I first used the pan for a couple of weeks, I had this to say about it:"The cooking surface is the slickest I have ever encountered, with no sticking whatsoever. Clean up is super easy, just wipe out with a cloth. I am also pleased that it heats so evenly. It works great on my smooth surface range. I love this pan!"Now, not so much. Ozeri needs to get their chemists working on this conundrum. This pan went from non-stick loveliness to so sticky that even bacon adheres to it's surface. It is unlikely to have been due to improper cleaning because the transformation took place mid-cooking session. I fried three eggs which didn't stick at all, flipped over with no problems, and then the fourth egg stuck. All other foods cooked on the surface since the first egg-sticking have firmly adhered like it was a completely non-treated fry pan, worse even, since using oils doesn't seem to keep food from sticking. The problem has just gotten worse. I read a suggestion by Ozeri that I rinse the pan in vinegar. Done. Didn't help. Previous to it's super sticky transformation, I babied this pan, pampered it, seasoned it according to the directions that came with the pan, washed it with gentle dish soap and a cloth, and used only silicone, rubber, or bamboo cooking implements. Perhaps a really good wash with a different dish soap is in order?On a positive note, it does still cook very evenly, even as it grabs hold of my food like an obsessed, bunny-boiling lover. (Do the young folks know about Fatal Attraction these days?) If I find a way to restore its previously amazing non-stick properties, I will update again.
summary: How I fixed my Ozeri Green Earth Frying Pan

So I purchased this primarily so I could use the more plentiful, cheaper K-cups in my Vue machine. When I first tried out the adapter, I made the mistake of just setting the K-cup into the adapter, presuming the machine would press it into place. Do not do this. You need to press the K-cup firmly down into the adapter until it is pierced by the bottom tube/syringe thingy. If you don't press the K-cup fully down into the adapter, the hole punctured on top will be punctured at an angle, creating more of a slice than a hole, and you'll get grounds in the coffee. Also, you need to remove the plastic lid, which is only used along with the use-your-own filter. This should be obvious, but since my adapter didn't really include any instructions, I can see some poor fellow thinking you need to close that lid onto a K-cup. Don't do that.I noticed that some brands of K-cup were tougher to use, since the bottom was more resistant to puncturing by the adapter. It's like some K-cups have slightly stronger plastic. Because of this, I suggest that when you push the Kcup down into the adapter, you place your thumbs on either side, along the rim, not pressing on the lid/seal, to prevent accidentally puncturing the seal. Better yet, press down on it with the palm of your hand to distribute force. Before you point out that such instructions should be obvious, recall that we're talking about people who may be using this thing for the first time before they've had their coffee. When placed correctly, the K-cups work fairly well. I could be crazy, but I swear that k-cups used in my Vue with the adapter do not produce as good coffee as they do in a K machine, but it could be psychological.So far as the filter attachment goes, it does ok for using your own coffee, but I noticed that it does allow a fair amount of grounds to pass through. Either they are passing through the filter or overflowing over it, I don't know. I am able to minimize it by not putting too much grounds in; I fill it maybe 2/3 of the filter level.In conclusion, it works, but can be a tad finicky. Sadly, there really aren't any other options I've seen for making K-cups in a Vue machine aside from home-grown techniques via rubber bands and so forth, so this is what ya get.

I had originally written a 5 star positive review for this frying pan, but after having used it for several months I discovered that it doesn't hold up. During the first few months, the frying pan performs flawlessly. Nothing sticks to it, including eggs. They simple slide right off and with no residue left behind, clean-up takes a few seconds.The directions state to do the following prior to using the pan for the first time. You spread a light coating of vegetable oil over the entire green surface of the pan. Next, you place the pan on your stove-top over medium heat. When it starts to smoke, remove it from the stove. Let it cool completely, than wipe away the excess oil with a cloth or paper towel. Repeat every 6 months.The problem is that the pan deteriorates significantly with use, thus even after repeating the seasoning process at 6 months or earlier, the pan becomes no better than a regular one. Eggs start sticking to the surface and it becomes very difficult to clean. In addition, the pan scratches easily, even when used with a rubber spatula. If there were some way for the manufacturer to design this pan for long-term use, it would be an excellent product. As it stands now, it's a waste of money.The bottom line is that while this is an excellent pan for the short-term, the long-term prospects are bad. You'll love using it when you first buy it, than be very upset after just a few months. Since this pan is fairly expensive, I would have to say that there are much better choices available.
